name: Eversource Energy
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated electric and natural-gas franchises across Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire plus New England's largest transmission network, with essential inelastic demand and a $26.5B 2026-2030 capital plan that grows rate base at regulated returns — a durable, visible compounding machine. Capped at 6 because regulators (PURA, DPU, NH PUC, FERC) set the allowed return so there is no pricing power beyond rate cases — FERC lowered transmission ROE to 9.57% in March 2026 — the plan is funded with debt (net debt $28,130M) plus recurring equity issuance (share count +2.25%/yr), and offshore-wind contingent liabilities and affordability pushback in CT/MA sit with the equity.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Durable New England regulated monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years (capex exceeds OCF; normalized base -$6.57/share, latest FY -$0.21/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided 5-7% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated electric and gas franchises in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire — captive, essential-service customers
Largest electric transmission network in New England, FERC-regulated formula-rate returns
$26.5B 2026-2030 regulated capital plan grows rate base, recovered through rates
Essential, inelastic demand through cycles; pure-play regulated pivot after offshore-wind exit
moat_against: Regulators cap returns — CT PURA, MA DPU, NH PUC and FERC set allowed ROE; FERC cut transmission ROE to 9.57% in March 2026
Growth is debt- plus equity-funded: net debt $28,130M and share count +2.25%/yr dilutes rate-base growth per share
Lingering offshore-wind contingent liabilities to GIP and Aquarion sale losses — charges recurred in 2024, 2025 and H1 2026
High customer rates and affordability politics in CT/MA constrain rate recovery for a $26.5B capital plan
